title: Trae Pricing 2026: Plans, Free Tier and Costs
summary: Trae pricing includes a free tier plus paid plans. See the specific cost of each option to select the right plan for your needs.
body_markdown:
## Where Activepieces fits next to Trae


Nothing about Activepieces changes Trae's price or your request count: its Free plan is $0 with 1,000 credits a month and unlimited flows, so the script Trae writes can run without drawing on your Trae allowance.


> Once overage exceeds the gap between tiers, the higher plan is the cheaper one.


If you pay for heavy model access daily, that spend stays where it's.


### Why Trae can't run automations by itself


Trae is a code editor with an AI assistant. It drafts the script, you test it, and then it sits in a project folder doing nothing.


Trae has no scheduler, no listener for incoming events, and no place to keep a workflow alive after you close the window. Every request spent on that script was spent on authoring, and none of it buys execution.


Filling that gap is Activepieces, whose core carries an MIT licence in the LICENSE file of its public GitHub repository, and whose 747 integrations are counted from the community integrations directory of that same open source monorepo, so you can self-host it.


A finished script goes in as a step, and the platform fires it from a clock-based schedule or from a webhook, which is a URL that other software calls when something happens.


*\[Illustration: Trae hands a finished script to Activepieces, an MIT-licensed core with 747 integrations, which runs it on a timer or a webhook.\]*


### How the two products bill


What to take from it: the two products bill for different things. Trae's limit is how many AI requests you make while writing.


Activepieces' cost is about how often the workflow runs, and where: 1 credit a run on the cloud plans, with Plus at $20 a month for 10,000 credits, so active users pay a predictable monthly fee instead of scaling charges.


That split is why a script you generate once can run thousands of times without touching your Trae quota.


When you self-host, part of the bill moves to your own server, a cost you can calculate from your own run volume rather than guess.


### How workflow credits compare to per-task billing?


Activepieces' pricing page counts a flow run as 1 credit however many steps it contains, where Zapier bills per task and Make per module, so a ten-step workflow costs the same as a two-step one.


The Free plan includes 1,000 credits a month, and Plus is $20 a month for 10,000 credits, then $0.007 a credit over, which means overages add up fast if you exceed your tier.


Run those figures against your own expected monthly executions, then settle these, in this order:


1. How your AI steps are rated: a fast model is 2 credits, a smart model 10 and a frontier model 20, unless you bring your own AI keys on Plus and up, where each AI step is 1 credit and the model cost goes to your own provider bill.
2. Whether the self-hosted edition carries the same limits as the hosted one, or drops some of them.
3. What happens past the included volume: a hard stop, or overage billing.
4. Whether any price shown requires contacting sales. If it does, treat the tier as unpriced until someone writes a number down.


Add the result to your Trae plan. That sum is your real bill.
